_comment: All Adventurers Guild innkeeper dialogue. tools/EspGen turns this into dialogue records (INFO FormIDs are pinned in dialogue.ids.json, which voice files are named after - never renumber). The voice pipeline reads the same file. Keep lines short: they will be voiced.
_liaisons: Optional 'whenGlobal': {global, <role>: lines} replaces a role's lines while that global is 1 (the DLL keeps it: AG_MissivesSolstheimGlobal = Raven Rock has the missive board of Missives - Worldspace Additions). The Guild keeps a counter only at the inn of each hold capital, the towns that have a Missives board. Only these innkeepers register, promote and open the counter. While registration / promotion is the Guild Hall's alone (2.0, MCM > Guild Hall, AG_HallRegistrationGlobal / AG_HallPromotionGlobal), no innkeeper offers it (no new lines outside the hall for now); an optional 'registerHall' / 'promoteHall' line (also inside 'afterQuest') would answer instead, sending the player to the hall. Optional per liaison: '<role>Ask' (their own fee ask), 'businessByRank' (business line by the player's rank: C, B, A, S; the plain 'business' line covers the ranks that have none), 'businessExtra' (more business lines for any rank) and 'businessByRankExtra' (one more for a rank); the game picks at random among the business lines that fit, 'afterQuest' {quest, <role>: lines} (replaces those lines once the quest is completed). 'replace': what they say handing over a replacement guild card (the topic is only offered to a member who carries no card; the fee is in the player's line, so there is no ask). 'successor' {of, quest, alias, ref, cell}: this NPC keeps the counter once the liaison they follow is dead, whoever runs the inn (with the Unofficial Patch Mikael takes the Bannered Mare over, not Ysolda). quest + alias = the hold's Dialogue quest and its Innkeeper alias ('Plugin|0xID', number): the game swaps the backup in when the innkeeper dies, which is how the DLL knows. ref = the successor's own reference; cell = the inn: they do Guild business only there, and 'away' is what they say anywhere else. The DLL adds them to AG_GuildLiaisonFaction, and every line of theirs waits for that.

businessExtra: Sit yourself down, adventurer. The stew can mind itself for a minute.
You've the look of someone with work on their mind. Out with it, then.

businessByRankExtra.S: The whole room went quiet when you came in, love. They'll pretend it didn't. What do you need?

liaisons.register: Welcome to the Adventurers Guild! Here's your guild card. The Companions will sneer, but the Guild pays on time, and the work's never dull.
liaisons.business: Guild business? Pull up a stool. Saadia, mind the bar.
liaisons.promoteAsk: Let's see what the ledger says about you. Well, well! You've earned your next rank. There's just the Guild's fee to make it official.
liaisons.promote: There, love. Congratulations. Here's your new card; now go and eat something hot before the next job finds you. It always does.
about: The Companions take the jobs that make a good song. Adventurers take the ones that need doing. Farmers know the difference.
liaisons.registerAsk: Looking to join the Adventurers Guild? Good, we could use new blood. There's a small fee to put your name down, that's all.
liaisons.stampedFirst: There you are, love. Whiterun's horse, right on your card. Show it around the shops. Some of them go easier on an adventurer whom the hold knows.

cardHandIn.dead: Ah. Then they won't be needing it. I'll close their page in the ledger and send word to their kin. Thank you for bringing it home.
cardHandIn.fallen: One of yours. I'm sorry, love, truly. I'll see the ledger put right and their family told. Sit. These are on the house, for those of you still standing.
cardHandIn.worn: I can't make out a name on this. Still, a card should come home. I'll send it on to the Adventurers Guild. Thank you.

liaisons.replace: Lost it already? Happens to the best of them. Here, a fresh one. Try to keep this one out of the mead.

businessExtra: Tell me you've brought something back. I love it when adventurers bring things back.
liaisons.registerAsk: Joining the Adventurers Guild? Smart. There's a small fee, and it's the best coin you'll spend this year.
liaisons.register: Welcome to the Adventurers Guild! Here's your guild card. You bring in the work, I'll see we both profit by it.
liaisons.business: Guild business? My favorite kind. What are you bringing me?
liaisons.promoteAsk: Let me look at your record. Oh, that's a healthy one. You've earned your next rank. There's the Guild's fee, and then it's yours.
liaisons.promote: Congratulations! I've updated your guild card. A higher rank means better-paying work. For both of us.
about: Bandits are bad for trade, and so are trolls. Every missive an adventurer finishes puts coin back in Whiterun's market.
liaisons.stampedFirst: Whiterun's stamp, on your card. Show it when you shop here. A merchant who knows what it means might find you a better price. I would.

cardHandIn.dead: Oh. I see. I'll mark the ledger and have word sent to their family. Nobody warns you about this part of the counter.
cardHandIn.fallen: They travelled with you? I'm sorry. I'll settle the ledger and write to their kin myself. Buy yourselves some drinks and I'll see their name is remembered properly.
cardHandIn.worn: There's no reading this one. I'll send it to the Adventurers Guild all the same. Somebody there may know it.

liaisons.replace: Lost your guild card? Replacements cost, I'm afraid. A merchant can't give away stock. Here you are.

businessExtra: Ah, back in one piece! That's worth a toast later. Business first, eh?
For an adventurer, friend, I always have time. The wine will keep.
liaisons.register: Welcome to the Adventurers Guild! Here's your guild card. Solitude's never short of work, and now you're first in line.
liaisons.business: Adventurers Guild business, friend? Sit, relax. Whatever chased you here stops at my doorway.
liaisons.promoteAsk: A step up? I'd say so. The East Empire clerks drink here, and they've stopped complaining about the roads. That's your doing. The Adventurers Guild asks its fee, and it's yours.
liaisons.promote: Congratulations, friend. Here's your new card. Tonight you sit, relax, and let somebody else's troubles wait at the door.
about: Solitude's the capital, so the work is as often a noble's quiet problem as a wolf on the road. Both pay. The noble pays better.
I've poured for adventurers who walked up the Embassy road and never came back for their change. I still have it, if they do.
liaisons.registerAsk: An adventurer wanting to sign on? Splendid! Solitude always has work for a capable blade. The Guild asks a small fee to join.
liaisons.stampedFirst: There, friend. Solitude's wolf, on your card. Show it around the shops. You may find the prices kinder.

cardHandIn.dead: Ah, that's a sad thing to carry. I'll close the ledger and see their family hears it gently. Thank you, friend.
cardHandIn.fallen: One of your own? I'm sorry, friend. Leave the ledger and the letters to me. Sit, all of you. These are on the house.
cardHandIn.worn: No name left on it. Well. I'll send it along to the Adventurers Guild. Better here than in a ditch.

liaisons.replace: Lost your card? Careless, but easily mended. There you are, good as new.

businessExtra: Oh, good, an adventurer. I was worried I might get to sit down.
liaisons.registerAsk: Joining the Adventurers Guild? Your funeral. There's a small fee first. There's always a fee.
liaisons.register: Welcome to the Adventurers Guild. Here's your guild card. Try not to die before your first job. It's bad for business.
liaisons.business: Guild business? Fine. Let's get it over with.
liaisons.promoteAsk: Let's see the ledger. Well, look at that. You've earned your next rank. The Guild wants its fee first, naturally.
liaisons.promote: Congratulations. I've updated your guild card. Go on, look pleased with yourself.
about: I ran errands for the old man my whole life. Now the Winking Skeever's mine, and so is the Adventurers Guild's counter. Be careful what you wish for.
liaisons.stampedFirst: Solitude's wolf. On your card. Flash it at the merchants. A few of them go soft for a stamped card. Don't ask me why.

cardHandIn.dead: Dead, then. Right. I'll strike the name and send the letter. My father used to do this part. I see why he drank.
cardHandIn.fallen: They were with you? I'm sorry. I mean that. I'll deal with the ledger. Drinks are on the house. Don't tell anyone I said so.
cardHandIn.worn: I can't read a word of this. I'll send it up the line. Someone at the Adventurers Guild is paid to squint.

liaisons.replace: Lost your guild card already? Of course you did. Here. That's coming out of your pocket, not mine.

businessExtra: Stamp the snow off first. Right. What does an adventurer want with me today?
You're back, and with all your fingers. More than some manage. Go on, then.
liaisons.register: Here's your guild card. You're an adventurer now, same as the ones who tramp snow up my stairs. Wipe your boots like they don't.
liaisons.business: Come in out of the wind. If it's Adventurers Guild business, I'm listening. If it's a drink, the great room's upstairs.
liaisons.promoteAsk: Moving up, you reckon. I hear things at this bar. Carters, guards, hunters off the steam fields. They've been saying your name. That'll do me. There's the fee.
liaisons.promote: It's done. You'll find the work gets colder and the pay gets better. That's Eastmarch for you.
about: Eastmarch work is trolls on the roads and ice wraiths off the mountains. Nothin' fancy. Nothin' magic, neither, and I'll thank you to keep it so.
Come back cold and you'll get the fire, bread and a bed. Come back bleeding and you'll get the same, but you'll mop the floor after.
liaisons.registerAsk: Adventurer, is it? Eastmarch eats them. Trolls on the roads, wraiths off the ice. If you still want in, the Adventurers Guild takes a fee.
liaisons.stampedFirst: The bear of Eastmarch, on your card. Don't smudge it. Show it to the traders, and some might charge you less. Not much else warms this city.

cardHandIn.dead: Dead, then. I'll mark the ledger and send word to whoever's left. Windhelm has had practice at that.
cardHandIn.fallen: One of yours. That's a hard road home. I'll see to the ledger and the letter. I don't pour for free, but sit by the fire and drink as long as you need.
cardHandIn.worn: I can't read the name. Snow's had it, or blood. I'll send it on to the Adventurers Guild.

liaisons.replace: Down a troll's gullet, I hope, and not just the back of a bed. Here's another, and it'll cost you.

businessExtra: Adventurer's work, is it? Let me wipe my hands, and I'm all yours.
liaisons.registerAsk: Looking to join the Adventurers Guild? Good for you, good for you. There's a small fee, I'm sorry to say.
liaisons.register: Welcome to the Adventurers Guild! Here's your guild card. Mind yourself out there, and come back for a hot meal.
liaisons.business: Guild business? Sit down by the fire, and we'll see to it.
liaisons.promoteAsk: Let me find my spectacles. There. Why, you've earned your next rank! There's the Guild's fee, and then it's done.
liaisons.promote: Congratulations! I've updated your guild card. I'm proud of you, I truly am.
about: Windhelm's cold, and the work's colder. Ice wraiths, trolls on the roads. Eat before you go out.
liaisons.stampedFirst: There now. Windhelm's bear, on your card. Show it at the market, mind. Some of the merchants take a little off for it.

cardHandIn.dead: Oh dear. I am sorry. I'll write it in the ledger and send word to their family. Thank you for bringing it.
cardHandIn.fallen: They were one of yours? Oh, I'm so sorry. I'll see to everything. Now sit, please. A drink for each of you, and not a coin.
cardHandIn.worn: I can't make out the name at all. I'll send it on to the Adventurers Guild. Somebody ought to have it.

liaisons.replace: Lost your guild card? Never mind, never mind. Here's a new one. Keep it somewhere dry.

businessExtra: Make it quick, adventurer. I've a room full of people who don't tip.
You, I don't mind seeing. You pay for your drinks. What do you need?
liaisons.register: Welcome to the Guild. Here's your card. Keep your hands out of other people's pockets and you'll do fine.
liaisons.business: Guild business. Good. At least one guild in Riften does its work in the open.
liaisons.promoteAsk: Talen, bring me the ledger. Well. You've been busy, and the Guild noticed. The fee, and the rank is yours.
liaisons.promote: Congratulations. Your guild card's updated. Try to stay alive long enough to enjoy it.
about: The Rift's got more bandits than honest folk, and the Black-Briars like it that way.
If a missive looks too easy in Riften, read it twice. Someone's usually getting paid to look away.
liaisons.registerAsk: You want to join the Adventurers Guild? Good. Riften needs honest blades more than most. There's a fee, of course.
liaisons.stampedFirst: There. Riften's mark, on your card. Show it to the merchants. A few might take less off you than they take off everyone else.

cardHandIn.dead: Dead. I'll close their page and send word to their kin. One less honest blade in the Rift.
cardHandIn.fallen: One of yours. I'm sorry. I'll see to the ledger and the letter. Talen, drinks for this table. On the house.
cardHandIn.worn: No name I can read. I'll send it on to the Adventurers Guild. It didn't deserve the canal.

liaisons.replace: Lost, or lifted? In Riften it's usually lifted. Here's a new one. Keep it somewhere your purse isn't.

businessExtra: One moment. There. The drinks can wait, and you have my full attention.
liaisons.registerAsk: You wish to join the Adventurers Guild? That is good. There is a small fee, as is the custom.
liaisons.register: Welcome to the Adventurers Guild. Here is your guild card. Keerava kept this counter with care. I will do the same.
liaisons.business: Guild business? Of course. I am at your service.
liaisons.promoteAsk: Allow me to consult the ledger. Yes. You have earned your next rank. There is the Guild's fee, and then it is yours.
liaisons.promote: Congratulations. I have updated your guild card. Keerava would have been pleased.
about: In Riften, not every job is posted on a board. The Adventurers Guild's work is honest. That is rarer here than it should be.
liaisons.stampedFirst: It is done. Riften's daggers are on your card. Show it to the merchants here. Some may ask a fairer price of you.

cardHandIn.dead: Then they are gone. I will close the ledger and send word to their family. Thank you for carrying it here.
cardHandIn.fallen: One of your own. I am sorry for your loss. I will see to the ledger. Please, sit. These drinks are on the house.
cardHandIn.worn: The name cannot be read. I will send it to the Adventurers Guild. It should not be left in the mud.

liaisons.replace: You have lost your guild card? In Riften, check your pockets twice. Here is another.

businessExtra: An adventurer! Good, good. Frabbi, watch the bar. No? Fine. I'll do both.
Step over here by the hearth, friend. The stone carries every word in this city.
liaisons.register: Welcome to the Guild. Your card, friend. Mind the Silver-Bloods, they own this inn and the Guild's rent too.
liaisons.business: Guild business, yes. Quickly now, before someone important walks in.
liaisons.promoteAsk: Let me check the ledger. You've earned your next rank, friend. Pay the fee and we'll make it official, quietly.
liaisons.promote: Congratulations. Your guild card's updated. Wear the new rank carefully in this city.
about: The Reach is Forsworn country. The Guild pays well out here, because not everyone comes back.
Anything you hear in Markarth, the Silver-Bloods heard first. Remember that.
liaisons.registerAsk: Joining the Guild? Welcome, friend. Quietly now, this is the Silver-Bloods' inn. There's a small fee to sign on.
liaisons.stampedFirst: There. Markarth's ram, on your card. Show it at the stalls, not to the Silver-Bloods. A merchant might charge you less for it.

cardHandIn.dead: Dead? In the Reach, I'm not surprised. I'll strike the name and write to the family. Quietly.
cardHandIn.fallen: One of yours. I'm sorry, friend. I'll handle the ledger. Here, drinks for your people. On the house. Don't tell Frabbi.
cardHandIn.worn: I can't read it. Half of what's found in the Reach is like that. I'll send it on to the Adventurers Guild.

liaisons.replace: Lost your card? In Markarth that's the least of what people lose. There, a new one.

businessExtra: Oh, you're back! And upright. Lovely. What can I do for you, dear?
Is it business, dear? Good. It's been all funerals and no news in here today.
liaisons.register: Welcome to the Guild. Here's your card. Falkreath has more graves than guests, so try not to add to them.
liaisons.business: Guild business. Good. Better you than the undertaker.
liaisons.promoteAsk: Let's see if the ledger has you marked for promotion or the graveyard. Promotion! Good for you. Pay the fee and I'll write it in.
liaisons.promote: Congratulations! Your guild card's updated. And you're still breathing. Rare, for Falkreath.
about: Half the missives in Falkreath end at the graveyard. The other half end there later.
liaisons.registerAsk: Signing on with the Guild? Brave of you. Falkreath will keep you busy. There's just a small fee first.

businessByRank.B: You've outlived most of the adventurers who drank here. Sit down. What do you need?

liaisons.stampedFirst: There you are, dear. Falkreath's stag, on your card. Show it at the shops. Folk here might give you a better price.

cardHandIn.dead: Oh. Another for the graveyard, then. I'll close the ledger and write to their family. Thank you, dear.
cardHandIn.fallen: Oh, one of yours. I'm so sorry, dear. Falkreath knows that grief. I'll see to the ledger. These are on the house, all of them.
cardHandIn.worn: I can't read the name, dear. I'll send it to the Adventurers Guild all the same. Someone may be waiting on it.

liaisons.replace: Oh, you've lost it? No harm done. Here's a new card, dear.

businessExtra: You came back out of the marsh. Not everybody does. What do you need, adventurer?
liaisons.register: Welcome to the Guild! Here's your card. Morthal's lucky to have you.
liaisons.business: Guild business. Come closer, folk in Morthal like to listen.
liaisons.promoteAsk: Let me check the ledger. Morthal doesn't see many rise this far, but you have. There's a small fee, then it's official.
liaisons.promote: Congratulations! I've updated your guild card. Morthal's proud of you, even if it won't say so.
about: Things come out of the marsh fog that don't belong in any bestiary. The Guild pays well for every one of them.
liaisons.registerAsk: The Guild? Out here? Well, Morthal could certainly use the help. There's a small fee to join.

businessByRank.C: You've been busy out there, haven't you? Morthal notices. What is it?

liaisons.stampedFirst: There. Morthal's mark, on your card. Show it to the shopkeepers. They might ask less of someone who's done this town some good.

cardHandIn.dead: Gone, then. I'll mark the ledger and send word to their people. Morthal has lost enough, but thank you for bringing it.
cardHandIn.fallen: One of yours? I'm sorry. Truly. I'll take care of the ledger. Sit down, all of you. The drinks are on the house.
cardHandIn.worn: The marsh has eaten the name off it. I'll send it to the Adventurers Guild anyway.

liaisons.replace: Lost in the marsh, I'd wager. Half of Morthal's belongings are. Here's a new card.

businessExtra: Adventurer. Good. Karita's songs can wait, and so can the dishes. What is it?
You've come in off the ice with something on your mind. Let's hear it.
liaisons.register: There, you're in. Here's your guild card. Nobody sleeps in Dawnstar lately anyway, might as well work.
liaisons.business: Guild business at this hour? Not like anyone's sleeping. Go on.
liaisons.promoteAsk: Karita, fetch the lamp. Well, look at that. You've earned your next rank. Pay the fee and I'll mark it down.
liaisons.promote: Congratulations. Your guild card's updated. Maybe now you'll sleep better than the rest of us.
about: The Pale's all ice and mines and giants. Miners post more work than anyone.
And the nightmares. Everyone in town's having them. If the Guild can fix that, I'll pay the bounty myself.
liaisons.registerAsk: Joining the Guild? Good. Dawnstar needs all the help it can get. Just the fee, and you're in.

afterQuest._comment: Waking Nightmare (Vaermina's nightmares on Dawnstar): once it is completed, these replace the lines that talk about them.
afterQuest.business: Guild business? Go on. Now that the nightmares are over, I can actually keep my eyes open for it.
afterQuest.register: There, you're in. Here's your guild card. The Pale always has work for a steady blade.
afterQuest.promote: Congratulations. Your guild card's updated. Drinks are on the house, now that we're all sleeping again.
about: The Pale's all ice and mines and giants. Miners post more work than anyone.
The nightmares are over, thank the gods. Now it's just the giants and the cold.

liaisons.stampedFirst: There. Dawnstar's star, on your card. Show it around the shops. Some of them might go easier on your purse.

cardHandIn.dead: Dead. I'll close their page and send the letter. I've written too many of those.
cardHandIn.fallen: One of your own. I'm sorry. I'll see to the ledger. Karita, drinks for these adventurers. On the house.
cardHandIn.worn: I can't read a name on it. I'll send it on to the Adventurers Guild. Somebody should.

liaisons.replace: Lost your card? It happens. Here's a new one, and the ledger still knows your name.

businessExtra: A customer and an adventurer, both at once! That's a busy day in Winterhold. What do you need?
Come and warm up first. Then you can tell me what the Adventurers Guild can do for you.
liaisons.register: Welcome to the Guild! Your card. The counter's the only thing in Winterhold still standing that isn't the College.
liaisons.business: Guild business. Most of it comes from the College, mages who won't leave their tower.
liaisons.promoteAsk: Haran, where did we put that book? Ah, you've earned a promotion! The Guild just wants its fee first.
liaisons.promote: Congratulations! Your guild card's updated. Most exciting thing to happen here since the Collapse.
about: Mages post the strangest missives. Ice wraith teeth, frost salts, things from the ruins.
liaisons.registerAsk: Want to join the Guild? Winterhold could use some excitement. There's a small fee to sign you up.
liaisons.stampedFirst: There! Winterhold's crown, on your card. Show it to the merchants. There aren't many, but they might charge you less.

cardHandIn.dead: Oh. That's a shame. I'll mark the ledger and write to their family. Winterhold knows about losing people.
cardHandIn.fallen: One of yours? I'm sorry, friend. I'll take care of the ledger. Haran! Drinks for everyone here. On the house.
cardHandIn.worn: No name left on it. The cold does that. I'll send it to the Adventurers Guild all the same.

liaisons.replace: Lost your card? Things have a way of vanishing in Winterhold. Here's another, friend.

businessExtra: A job done, and a story to go with it. That's my favorite kind of customer.
Let me finish pouring this. There. Now, what does the adventurer need from Geldis?
liaisons.register: I know everyone in Raven Rock, and they know me. Now they'll know you too. It's in the ledger. Take your guild card, adventurer.
liaisons.business: This end of the bar, then, away from the sujamma. Adventurers Guild business goes better sober. Mostly.
liaisons.promoteAsk: Sit. I want to read this page properly. Azura knows I've poured for people who did less and bragged more. The Adventurers Guild takes its fee, and I get to write in the new letter.
liaisons.promote: There. I've changed the letter on your guild card. I've changed it in the story I tell about you, too.
about: There's no missive board here. People with a problem tell their barkeep, and their barkeep tells an adventurer. It's an older system.
There's a missive board up by Morvayn Manor now. Half of Raven Rock still tells their barkeep first, and their barkeep tells an adventurer. It's an older system.

liaisons.registerAsk: You want to sign with the Adventurers Guild in Raven Rock? Most people who land here are trying to leave. I like you already, outlander. There's a fee. There's always a fee.
liaisons.stampedFirst: House Redoran's mark, on your card. Show it to Raven Rock's traders. Some will take a little off for a face the town can vouch for.

cardHandIn.dead: Ah. Then this is where their story ends. I'll close the ledger and send word to their kin. I'll tell it kindly.
cardHandIn.fallen: One of yours, sera? I am sorry. I'll see to the ledger. Sit. The sujamma is on the house, and we'll drink to them.
cardHandIn.worn: No name I can read. Ash does that. I'll send it on to the Adventurers Guild, and wonder whose it was.

liaisons.replace: A lost guild card always comes with a story, and I collect those. No? Then it's the fee, and I'll make one up for you.

_staff: Other people who work at a guild inn point you to their rep. whileAlive / whenDead = an NPC editor ID the line needs alive / dead (the innkeeper it names; their successor). unlessInFaction {ref, faction} = the line is skipped while that reference is in that faction (Mikael's 'I got the inn' line, if Ysolda is the innkeeper after all).

staff.line: Guild business goes through Hulda. She's the Guild's rep here.
Guild business goes through Ysolda now. She took the counter over when Hulda passed.
My father runs the Guild's counter. Talk to him.
Keerava handles anything to do with the Guild.
Guild? Talk to my husband. That's his business, not mine.
My father keeps the Guild's counter. I just sing.
The Adventurers Guild? That was Kleppr's ledger, not mine. I've an inn to run on my own now. Try the counter in another hold.
Dagur kept the Adventurers Guild's ledger. I can pour your mead and rent you a bed, but the counter closed with him.
Jonna kept the Adventurers Guild's counter. There's no one to keep it now. I could sing you something about it?
Valga handled the Adventurers Guild's business. With her gone there's no counter in Falkreath. You'll have to ride to another hold.

_referrals: Innkeepers outside the hold capitals: no counter, but they know where to send you.

referrals.line: Guild business goes to one of the city inns. The Bannered Mare in Whiterun is the nearest one from here.
referrals.lineHall: Guild business? Up the hill. They've a whole hall for it.

referrals.line: I just run an inn. Try the Bannered Mare in Whiterun.
Ivarstead's too small for a Guild counter. Try the Bee and Barb in Riften.
Rorikstead's a farming town. For the Guild you want the Bannered Mare in Whiterun.
The Winking Skeever in Solitude handles Guild business. Just follow the road across the bridge.
No Guild counter in Kynesgrove. Ask in Windhelm.
Nightgate's a waystation, friend, not a Guild house. Windhelm's your best bet.
No Guild counter out here. The Silver-Blood Inn in Markarth is closest.
The Guild keeps its counter at Candlehearth Hall. Nords prefer their business kept among Nords.

_generic: Any other innkeeper, including ones added by other mods (anyone in JobInnkeeperFaction), unless they are travelling with the player as a follower.
generic: The Adventurers Guild keeps its counters in the hold capitals, near the missive boards. You won't find one out here.
genericHall: No Guild counter here. Try the guild hall in Riverwood, or an inn in one of the hold capitals.
_stampKeepers: Hold stamps (1.5.0). 'stamped' on a liaison: what she says, unasked, as her counter closes after she has stamped the card (an Idle line the DLL has her say, locked by AG_StampSayGlobal). 'replaceStamped': her reply to the replacement request when her hold's stamp is earned (the new card is stamped at once). stampKeepers: whoever takes over an inn whose counter closed with its liaison keeps the liaison's stamp and puts it on a card on request, nothing else; 'of' is the dead liaison. The DLL marks the keeper (AG_StampDueFaction) while the stamp is earned, not on the card, and the card is in hand.

stampKeepers.line: Kleppr's stamp? It's under the bar. There. Markarth's ram, on your card. That is all I do for the Adventurers Guild.
Father's stamp. I couldn't bring myself to put it away. Hold your card flat. There. Dawnstar's star.
Dagur's stamp is still here. He'd want it used. There, Winterhold's crown, on your card.
Jonna left me the inn, and the stamp. Some say I am better with the stamp than the lute. There! Morthal's mark!
Valga's stamp? I kept it. Come closer, this needs a steady hand. There. Falkreath's stag, and it suits you.

_cardHandIn: Other adventurers' guild cards (1.5.0, MemberCards.cpp). On a liaison, cardHandIn: her reply when cards are handed in at the counter, by the weightiest of them (AG_CardCaseGlobal: 1 the owner lives, 2 is dead, 3 fell as one of the player's party, 4 only worn cards); drinks = whether she stands the party a round for the third.
_showCard: Show Guild Card (1.5.0): a member carrying the card can show it where vanilla asks the player to talk their way in. No vanilla line is overridden: each reply is ADDED to a vanilla choice, which it takes over when vanilla's own replies before it do not apply (tools/EspGen/Program.cs has the detail). college: Faralda, in place of '(Persuade)', any rank ('E' for a rank E member, 'other' for the rest), and she goes on into her own vanilla welcome. treasury: Rhiada, in place of '(Persuade)', rank C and up. orcs: a stronghold's gate guard, rank A and up, in each voice of 'orcVoices': in place of 'I go where I please, Orc.' at the first meeting, and as a topic of our own in his menu after it.

showCard.prompt: I'm with the Adventurers Guild. (Show Guild Card)
showCard._orcsPrompt: The player's line at an Orc stronghold, in both places it appears. Only rank A and up are offered it, so it says so: being 'with the Guild' is not what gets anyone past this gate.
showCard.orcsPrompt: I'm a high-rank adventurer. (Show Guild Card)

E: The Adventurers Guild? May I see your card?
Newly stamped, I see. Forgive me, I took you for another sightseer. The Adventurers Guild vouches for its own, and that will serve in place of a test.
other: The Adventurers Guild? May I see your card?
A ranked adventurer. Forgive me. I should not ask you to prove yourself on a doorstep.

showCard.treasury: Oh, you're with the Adventurers Guild! I'm so sorry, I didn't realize. The Silver-Bloods hold the lease on your counter, so that's family business. Head right in.
showCard.orcs: That card says you have bled for your rank, outlander. Malacath honors strength that is proven. You are no Orc, but you have earned a place at our fire. Enter.
showCard._added: riften: the north gate guard, in place of '(Persuade)' for a member whose Speech would not pass it. whiterun: the gate guard, in the place of the Riverwood line for a member Riverwood did not send. robber: the roadside thief, in place of '(Intimidate)' by Guild rank alone, B backs off, A and S beg; 'voices' are the voice types the encounter can use.
riften: The Adventurers Guild? Show me your card.
Huh. That's the real thing. Sorry. Forget I said anything about a tax, adventurer. Let me get that gate unlocked.
whiterun: Adventurers Guild? Let's see your card, then.
Stamped and sealed. Beg your pardon, adventurer. My orders are to keep strangers out, not the Adventurers Guild. Go on in.

robber.prompt: You're robbing a ranked adventurer of the Adventurers Guild. Walk away.
robber.B: A ranked adventurer? Right. Wrong traveler. No harm done, eh? On your way.
robber.AS: Gods, I didn't know! I've heard what your kind does to giants. Please, I'm sorry. Don't kill me!

prompts.register: I'd like to register with the Adventurers Guild.
prompts.rankings: Could I see the party rankings?
prompts.promote: I'd like to apply for promotion.
prompts.about: What's Guild work like around here?
prompts.stampAsk: I've earned this hold's stamp for my guild card. (Show Guild Card)
prompts.cardHandIn: I have a guild card to hand in.
prompts.replace: I've lost my guild card. I need a replacement.

_nofee: What a guild liaison says when the player picks register/promote without the fee in hand (no Goodbye; voiced per liaison voice type).

nofee.register: Joining the Guild takes a small fee. Come back when you can cover it.
nofee.promote: You've earned it, no question. But the Guild still wants its fee. Come back with the coin.
nofee.replace: A new card costs coin. Come back when you can cover it.

_ask: The liaison names the fee before registering / promoting; the player then chooses to pay or not (voiced per liaison voice type). A liaison's own "<role>Ask" line (promoteAsk: checks the ledger, congratulates, then the fee) replaces this for them; their "<role>" line is then what they say once paid.

ask.register: There's a small fee to join the Adventurers Guild. Will you pay it?
ask.promote: The Guild charges a fee to see a promotion through. Will you pay it?

later.register: Suit yourself. The Guild will be here when you're ready.
later.promote: As you like. The rank will be waiting for you.
